facts.text: Springfield was founded in 1801 by James Demint, a former Kentucky teamster who named it after Springfield, Massachusetts.
The land that became Springfield was ceded to the United States by the Shawnee under the 1795 Treaty of Greenville, six years before the city was founded.
Wittenberg University, a private liberal arts college, has called Springfield home since its founding in 1845.
The last passenger train left Springfield on April 30, 1971, a remnant of the New York Central’s Ohio State Limited on the Cincinnati–Columbus–Cleveland route.
The Little Miami Scenic Trail, a nearly 80‑mile paved rail‑trail, starts in Springfield’s Buck Creek Scenic Trail head and winds south to Newtown.
The Clark County Heritage Center houses the county historical society museum, library, and archives, preserving Springfield’s rich local history.
